classification.difficultyReason: Derive the supplied completed-square form of the discriminant and use its positive lower bound to classify the roots for every real p.

content.prompt:
Show that the discriminant of $x^2-(p+1)x+p-1=0$ is

$$\Delta=(p-1)^2+4$$

and hence discuss the roots of $x^2-(p+1)x+p-1=0$ for real values of $p$.

answer.short: Two distinct real roots for every real $p$, since $\Delta=(p-1)^2+4>0$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=[-(p+1)]^2-4(1)(p-1)\\\Delta&=p^2-2p+5\\\Delta&=(p-1)^2+4\end{align*}$$

Since $(p-1)^2\ge 0$ for real $p$, $\Delta\ge 4>0$. The equation has two distinct real roots for every real $p$.
